Have a long audio file — lecture, podcast, training — and want to split it into **30-minute parts**?\
Here are three easy ways to do it on Linux:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1️⃣ Using FFmpeg (fastest and best)

If you like the terminal, **FFmpeg** is a powerful tool that can do this in one line.

### Install FFmpeg

```{bash}
# sudo apt update
# sudo apt install ffmpeg
```

Check that it's installed:

```{bash}
# ffmpeg -version
```

Split the audio

```{bash}
# ffmpeg -i input.mp3 -f segment -segment_time 1800 -c copy output_%03d.mp3 
```

Explanation:

-   input.mp3: your audio file

-   segment_time 1800: split every 1800 seconds = 30 minutes

-   output\_%03d.mp3: output files will be named output_000.mp3, output_001.mp3, etc.

Example:

```{bash}
# ffmpeg -i lecture.mp3 -f segment -segment_time 1800 -c copy lecture_part_%03d.mp3
```

Tip: works for .mp3, .wav, .m4a, and more - just change the extension.

## Using Audacity (GUI option)

If you prefer a graphical interface, Audacity is an excellent open-source audio editor.

Install Audacity bash Copy Edit sudo apt install audacity Steps: Open the audio file in Audacity

Go to Analyze → Label Sounds... or manually place labels every 30 minutes

Go to File → Export → Export Multiple

Choose the format you want (mp3, wav, etc.)

Audacity will export each labeled segment as a separate file

## Bonus Tip: Automatic Transcription

If you're working with **lectures, interviews, or podcasts**, you might also want to **transcribe** the audio.

One great tool I've found is [TurboScribe.ai](https://turboscribe.ai/dashboard) — it works well for long audio and is easy to use.

> After splitting your audio into 30-minute parts, you can upload each part to TurboScribe.ai and get clean text transcripts.
